title: R20 v2: document every new scheduler, routing, allocation, strategy, speculation and promotion key in pool.toml at its in-code default, and carry the executor/review prompt rules onto the goal branch
spec:
v2: the v1 spec text contained a literal double-brace placeholder that the prompt renderer rejects; this text spells it out in words instead. Why: the roadmap modules merged in this goal read their configuration from pool.toml tables with defaults in code ([scheduler] duration_*/reserve_imminent/concurrency_mode/merge_pressure_*/jev_*; [jev.routing] max_adjustment, evidence_floor_n; [jev.points]; [allocation]; [strategy]; [speculation]; [promotion]). Nothing in pool.toml shows them, so an operator cannot see what is tunable or which mode a feature runs in (brief P15/P16: configuration and activation state must be visible). The Planner also changed three prompts on the main checkout (unittest.TestCase and _harness rules for executors, JSON-only review verdicts) that the goal branch must carry so the PR is self-contained.
What (config and prompt text only; no Python):
1. .orchestrator/pool.toml: add the keys below with exactly the in-code defaults and a one-line comment each; behaviour must not change (a test asserts the parsed values equal the module defaults). Under the existing [scheduler] table: duration_mode = "empirical", duration_min_samples = 5, duration_trim = 0.1, reserve_imminent = true, concurrency_mode = "adaptive", merge_pressure_mode = "observe", merge_queue_elevated = 3, merge_queue_saturated = 5, merge_conflicts_saturated = 2, jev_mode = "shadow", jev_max_pairs = 8, jev_cache_ttl_s = 3600, jev_cache_max_entries = 200. Under [jev.routing]: max_adjustment = 0.25, evidence_floor_n = 10. New tables: [jev.points] scout_necessity = "shadow", context_escalation = "shadow", review_escalation = "shadow", planner_relaunch = "shadow"; [allocation] mode = "shadow", min_samples = 5, latency_weight_usd_per_hour = 2.0, critical_factor = 1.0, non_critical_factor = 0.25; [strategy] mode = "shadow", min_samples = 10; [speculation] mode = "off", min_fix_round_p = 0.5, min_samples = 5, min_retry_cost_usd = 1.0; [promotion] min_samples = 20. Read each module (duration, capacity, concurrency, merge_pressure, jev_sched, jev_route, jev_points, allocation, strategy, speculation, promotion) to confirm the default names and values before writing; if a module's default differs from this list, the module wins and the spec value is corrected in the file with a note in the commit message.
2. .orchestrator/prompts/execute.md: after the line beginning "No new dependencies" insert, verbatim: "Tests: this repo runs unittest, not pytest. Every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name must be a method `def test_name(self)` inside a `unittest.TestCase` subclass in that file, named exactly as listed. Module-level `def test_*` functions and pytest fixtures (tmp_path, monkeypatch) are not collected and fail the gate; use tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and unittest.mock instead. Every tests/test_*.py begins with `import _harness` exactly like the existing tests (tests/_harness.py points ORCH_ROOT at one shared temporary root for the whole suite); never import it under another module path or create a second orchestrator state root, or unrelated hook and memory tests in the same run fail." placed before that "No new dependencies" line.
3. .orchestrator/prompts/fix-delta.md: after the "the assertion_lines placeholder line (the template line that consists of that name wrapped in double curly braces)" line insert, verbatim: "Tests: this repo runs unittest, not pytest. A failure "missing: test not defined" or "not collected by unittest" means the named test must be a `def test_name(self)` method inside a `unittest.TestCase` subclass in that file; module-level functions and pytest fixtures (tmp_path) are not collected. Use tempfile.TemporaryDirectory."
4. .orchestrator/prompts/review.md: after the "Return ONLY JSON" line insert, verbatim: "Your entire final message must be that one JSON object: no prose before or after it, no markdown code fences. Put any explanation inside a "summary" string field of the same object. A message with text outside the JSON object is not parseable and fails the review."
Tests (unittest.TestCase methods, tests/test_pool.py): parse .orchestrator/pool.toml with tomllib and assert the listed keys exist with the listed values and that [scheduler].mode, [jev.routing].mode stay "shadow" and [speculation].mode is "off".
acceptance: tests/test_pool.py::test_pool_toml_documents_roadmap_defaults — tomllib parse of .orchestrator/pool.toml yields every listed key with the listed default, [scheduler].mode and [jev.routing].mode shadow, [speculation].mode off
the three prompt files contain the inserted paragraphs verbatim (grep for 'unittest.TestCase', 'import _harness' and 'no markdown code fences' succeeds) and .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

constraints.interface_contract: pool.toml keys and values exactly as listed unless a module default differs; prompt insertions verbatim; no Python module changes
